land.text: the Milesian and Teian colonies on the Kerch strait (Panticapaeum, Nymphaion, Theodosia, Phanagoria, Hermonassa)

predecessors.note: The Archaeanactid union of the strait's Greek cities c. 480; the Bosporan Kingdom page dates 'the first Bosporan state' 480–438.

land.text: the Kerch peninsula, Theodosia and Taman — 'the remnants of the Bosporan Kingdom'

successors.note: 'absorbed into the Roman Empire by Justinian I' c. 527 after the revolt against the Hunnic ruler Gordas.

capitals.name: Panticapaeum
capitals.note: Infobox capital; Kerch. Phanagoria was 'the eastern capital' on the Taman side (Phanagoria page).

rulers.name: Archaeanax (Archaeanactids)
rulers.note: The list gives 'Archaeanax: c. 480 BC–?'; the Bosporan Kingdom page has the Archaeanactid 'first Bosporan state' 480–438.

rulers.name: Mithridates VI of Pontus (with Machares as viceroy)
rulers.note: Not in the king list: Paerisades V 'left his kingdom to Mithridates' (Bosporan Kingdom page, infobox Pontus 107–63 BC); the Spartocid page ends the dynasty in 108 with Saumacus.

rulers.name: Pharnaces II
rulers.note: Pharnaces II of Pontus page: king of Bosporus 63–47.

rulers.name: Asander
rulers.note: Asander page: in charge from 47, recognised by Augustus between 27 and 17, died 17 BC.

rulers.name: Dynamis (with Scribonius, then Polemon I of Pontus 16–8 BC)
rulers.note: Dynamis page: ruled alone 8 BC–AD 7/8; the king list has Aspurgus from 8/10.

rulers.name: Polemon II of Pontus and Gepaepyris
Cotys I
rulers.note: Cotys I page: installed by Claudius in 45, deposed by Nero in 63; the king list gives 46–78.

rulers.name: Douptounos (attested 483)
rulers.note: Rhescuporis VI page: 'the next well-attested king is Douptounos', inscription widely dated 483; no rulers are known between 341 and 483.

correction.text: Cliopatria's -404 shape: Panticapaeum and the Greek towns of the Kerch peninsula, back-dated to the Archaeanactid union of c. 480

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria starts the Bosporus in 404; the page has 'the first Bosporan state' from 480 and Spartocus I from 438. Nymphaion, an Athenian base c. 444, is inside this shape though it was 'annexed to the Bosporan Kingdom by the end of the century' (ledger -405); the Delian League dossier carves it out until then.
Kerch peninsula only (1,764 km2), -404..-384. Correct for the Spartocids before Leukon I: Sindica and Theodosia are still outside; Nymphaion is already inside (annexed by the end of the 5th century).

correction.text: the -366 shape without Theodosia: the Kerch peninsula plus the Taman peninsula and Gorgippia

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria repeats the Kerch-only shape for -383..-367, but 'Sindica was annexed by the Bosporan Kingdom during the reign of Leucon I, probably in the 380s BC' (Leukon I 389–349; Gorgippos co-ruler at Gorgippia from 389 on the Spartocid page; Phanagoria conquered 'in the early 4th century BC'). Theodosia was only taken c. 360 (ledger), hence the subtraction.

Kerch, Theodosia and Taman (6,621 km2), -366..-231. Theodosia was 'besieged in 365 and 360' and annexed (ledger gain -360, six years into the span — accepted). The Azov shore and Tanais are not yet included, matching Tanais' foundation 'late in the 3rd century BC'; the Spartocid page's claim that Paerisades I (349–310) 'took Tanais' disagrees and is recorded in the notes.

Adds the Azov shore to Tanais at the Don mouth (24,828 km2), -230..-92. The page: Tanais 'at the eastern edge of the territory of the kings of Bosporus', founded late 3rd century. The Bosporan Kingdom page's extent ('eastern half of Crimea and the Taman peninsula … to Tanais') matches.

correction.text: the -230/-63 shape unchanged: the kingdom under Mithridates VI of Pontus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe filling Cliopatria's gap -91..-64, during which the Bosporus was Mithridates VI's (Paerisades V 'left his kingdom to Mithridates'; infobox 'Pontus 107–63 BC'; Machares 'viceroy of Cimmerian Bosporus'). Drawn as the Bosporan state under Pontic tint via the ledger's vassal pair -107..-63; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Pontus shapes for these years overlap it and should be trimmed by the Pontus dossier.

correction.text: the -63 shape without Phanagoria, which Pompey declared independent in 63

keyframe_review.note: -63..67. At the keyframe's start Phanagoria had revolted against Mithridates, 'allied with the Roman Republic' and was declared 'independent' by Pompey; it is back under Polemon I, who renamed it Agrippia (ledger -16, confidence 1). The shape's last five years (63–67) were the Roman interlude under Nero ('part of the Roman Province of Moesia Inferior from 63 to 68'), recorded as an occupation in the ledger rather than by cutting the span.

correction.text: the -63 shape again: the kingdom restored to Rhescuporis II by Galba in 68

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe filling Cliopatria's gap 68..77; Galba restored the kingdom in 68 and nothing on the pages changes the borders before the 78 shape.

correction.text: the 78 shape without Roman Chersonesus (Sevastopol, 35 km) and the Crimean interior of the Late Scythians (Simferopol, 60 km)

keyframe_review.note: 78..370 (40,040 km2, all of Crimea). Chersonesus 'was subject to Rome and received a garrison from the middle of the 1st century BC until the 370s AD' and should stay out of the kingdom for the whole span. The Crimean interior (Scythian Neapolis, occupied to the second half of the 3rd century AD) only became Bosporan after Sauromates II's campaign of 193 (ledger gain); the correction holds at the keyframe's start year.
371..372. Chersonesus was Roman until the Huns took it in the 370s; otherwise accepted. Cliopatria ends the kingdom here; the pages do not (see cimmerian-bosporus_373).

correction.text: the -366 core (Kerch peninsula, Theodosia, Taman) — the kingdom's reduced extent under Gothic and Hunnic overlordship; borders unknown

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Bosporan Kingdom page runs to c. 527 ('absorbed into the Roman Empire by Justinian I'); Rhescuporis VI's page: Goths 'c. 380', then 'likely … a Hunnic invasion', a king Douptounos attested 483, and 'no evidence' that the kingdom was destroyed under Rhescuporis VI. The extent is a guess at the historical core and is marked soft in certainty; the Hun and Gothic dossiers may overlay it.

region.text: Panticapaeum and the Greek towns of the Kerch peninsula

ledger.note: c. 480: the Archaeanactids unite the cities of the strait — 'the first Bosporan state lasted from 480-438 BC'; the king list opens with 'Archaeanax: c. 480 BC'. Cliopatria's 404 start is a century late.
438: Spartocus I (438–431 on the Bosporan page, 438–433 on the Spartocid page and king list) founds the Spartocid dynasty, which rules to 108.

By the end of the 5th century: Nymphaion, Athens' 'principal military base in the region ca. 444 BC', 'was annexed to the Bosporan Kingdom by the end of the century' (Gylon's betrayal during the Peloponnesian War). Placed at 405, the last years of the war, at confidence 1.

region.text: the Taman peninsula and the Kuban mouth (Sindica: Phanagoria, Hermonassa, Gorgippia) — the -366 shape less the -383 shape and Theodosia

ledger.note: 380s: 'Sindica was annexed by the Bosporan Kingdom during the reign of Leucon I, probably in the 380s BC'; the native kings (Hecataeus, Octamasades) were deposed and Leukon's brother Gorgippos governed from Gorgippia (co-ruler 389–349 on the Spartocid page). Phanagoria page: 'in the early 4th century BC' the kingdom 'conquered much of Sindica, including the independent polis of Phanagoria'. Placed at Leukon's accession.
360: Theodosia, a Milesian colony, 'besieged in 365 and 360' and annexed by Leukon I; the Bosporan Kingdom page has Leucon (387–347) take Theodosia after Satyrus' siege.
310: war of succession after Paerisades I's death — Satyros II (311–310) and Prytanis (310–309) against their brother Eumelos.
309: 'Eumelus won' the succession war and ruled 309–304.

region.text: the Azov shore up to Tanais at the Don mouth — the -230 shape less the -366 shape

ledger.note: Late 3rd century: Tanais 'founded late in the 3rd century BC, by merchant adventurers from Miletus' at 'the eastern edge of the territory of the kings of Bosporus'; Cliopatria adds the Azov shore in 230. The Spartocid page instead has Paerisades I (349–310) take Tanais; the page names no previous holder, so the counterpart is the Maeotian hinterland at confidence 1.

107: Paerisades V 'left his kingdom to Mithridates' (infobox: 'Pontus 107–63 BC'); the Spartocid page ends the dynasty in 108 with Saumacus' revolt, which Diophantus put down. Drawn in Pontic tint until Mithridates' death.

Winter 66: Mithridates 'fled to the lands north of the Black Sea', killed his viceroy Machares and ruled from Panticapaeum himself; the capital does not move, the court does — recorded for the compiler's timeline only.
63: 'Pharnaces II of Pontus, led a rebellion against his father'; Mithridates 'withdrew to the citadel in Panticapaeum, where he committed suicide'.
63: Pharnaces II, king of Bosporus 63–47; Pompey 'named him a friend and ally' — the Roman client kingdom begins (Bosporan Kingdom infobox 'Roman client 63 BC–AD 63').
63: Phanagoria, which had risen against Mithridates and 'allied with the Roman Republic', was declared by Pompey 'to be independent' and later 'withstood a siege by Pharnaces II'.
48: while Caesar fought Pompey, Pharnaces 'seized Colchis, Lesser Armenia' and Pontus.
47: defeated by Caesar at Zela; Pharnaces fled to the Bosporus, where Asander had revolted, and was killed.
47: Asander, left 'in charge of the Bosporan Kingdom', revolts and takes the throne; 'Sometime between 27 and 17 BC, Augustus formally recognised Asander as king'.

17: Asander dies; Dynamis rules, briefly with Scribonius (killed), then with Polemon I of Pontus by Augustus' arrangement ('not … before 17/16 BC'); Polemon 'ruled until 8 BC'; Dynamis alone 8 BC–AD 7/8, then Aspurgus, founder of the Tiberian-Julian line of client kings.
c. 16: Polemon 'sacked Tanais' and renamed Phanagoria Agrippia, so the city was back in the kingdom by his reign; the pages do not date its return, hence confidence 1 at Polemon's accession.
45: Claudius installs Cotys I in place of his brother Mithridates III (42–46 on the king list).
63: Nero deposes Cotys I; the kingdom 'incorporated as a part of the Roman Province of Moesia Inferior from 63 to 68'.
68: Galba restores the kingdom under Rhescuporis II (68–93).

region.text: the Crimean interior around Scythian Neapolis (Simferopol), without Roman Chersonesus

ledger.note: 193: 'Sauromates II finished a military campaign against the Scythians and Sirachi tribes'; the Bosporan Kingdom page: under Sauromates II the kingdom 'included all the territories of the Crimean Peninsula' except Roman Chersonesus.
330: Tanais 'devastated by Goths AD 330' — the Don mouth lost; the Goths polity in Cliopatria ends in 206, so the counterpart is a slug without a shape at this date.

region.text: western and central Crimea and the Azov–Don shore — the 371 shape less the -366 core

ledger.note: 370s: the Huns take Chersonesus 'in the 370s AD' and the steppe; Cliopatria ends the kingdom in 372. The pages keep a Bosporan state on the strait (Goths 'took power over at least parts of the Bosporan Kingdom c. 380', then Huns), so only the Crimean west and the Azov shore are dropped here, at confidence 1.

region.text: the Kerch peninsula, Theodosia and Taman

ledger.note: c. 527: 'following a revolt against the Hunnic ruler Gordas … Justinian I sent an army to place the Bosporus under Roman rule' (Bosporan Kingdom infobox: disestablished c. AD 527).

wars.name: Sieges of Theodosia
wars.note: 'Theodosia was besieged in 365 and 360' (Spartocid page); the Bosporan Kingdom page has Satyrus begin the siege and Leucon take the city.

wars.name: Bosporan war of succession

zones.text: the Kuban country east of the strait

wars.outcome: Eumelos defeats his brothers Satyros II and Prytanis and rules 309–304.

wars.name: Mithridatic Wars (Bosporan theatre)
wars.outcome: Mithridates VI dies at Panticapaeum (63); Pharnaces II recognised by Pompey as 'friend and ally'; Phanagoria independent.
wars.note: Mithridates fled north 'in the winter of 66 BC'; Pharnaces' rebellion 'In 63 BC'.

wars.name: Pharnaces II's Anatolian war
wars.outcome: Caesar's victory at Zela (47); Pharnaces killed by Asander's revolt; Asander king.

wars.name: Sauromates II's Scythian war
wars.outcome: 'In 193, Sauromates II finished a military campaign against the Scythians and Sirachi tribes'; all Crimea except Chersonesus under the kingdom.
wars.note: The start year (186) is the page's 'perhaps'.

certainty.note: Archaeanactid period: one sentence on the page; extent assumed equal to Cliopatria's -404 shape.
Spartocid kings well dated (two pages agree within a few years); borders from Cliopatria plus Sindica, Theodosia and Tanais.
Pontic period: the kingdom is a possession of Mithridates VI; overlap with Cliopatria's Kingdom of Pontus shapes.
Roman client kingdom with a near-continuous king list; the Crimean interior's date of acquisition (193) and Chersonesus' status are the open points.
'the last well-known king' dies in 341; Gothic control c. 380, a Hunnic period, one king attested in 483, absorption by Justinian c. 527. Extent unknown; drawn as the -366 core.

sources.title: Bosporan Kingdom
sources.note: Infobox c. 438 BC – c. AD 527, capital Panticapaeum, Roman client 63 BC–AD 63 and 68–527; 'first Bosporan state lasted from 480-438 BC'; extent 'eastern half of Crimea and the Taman peninsula' to 'Tanais at the mouth of the Don'; Sauromates II 'included all the territories of the Crimean Peninsula'; 'part of Moesia Inferior from AD 63 to 68'; Goths c. 380; Justinian 527.

sources.title: Spartocid dynasty
sources.note: 438–108 BC; Leukon I 389–349 with Gorgippos co-ruler at Gorgippia; Theodosia besieged 365 and 360 and annexed; Paerisades I married Komosarye and 'took Tanais'; Saumacus killed Paerisades V (108).

sources.title: List of Bosporan kings
sources.note: Ruler list used for identity.rulers (Archaeanax c. 480 … Rhescuporis VI 314–341); 'After several successive periods of rule by groups such as the Sarmatians, Alans, Goths and Huns' the remnants were 'absorbed into the Roman Empire by Justinian I' after 'a revolt against the Hunnic ruler Gordas'.

sources.title: Tanais
sources.note: 'Founded late in the 3rd century BC, by merchant adventurers from Miletus'; 'at the eastern edge of the territory of the kings of Bosporus'; devastated by Goths AD 330; 47.26889N 39.335E.

sources.title: Sauromates II
sources.note: r. 172–210; 'In 193, Sauromates II finished a military campaign against the Scythians and Sirachi tribes'.

sources.title: Chersonesus
sources.note: Heraclean colony; called in Mithridates VI and Diophantus c. 110 BC; 'subject to Rome and received a garrison from the middle of the 1st century BC until the 370s AD' when captured by the Huns.

sources.title: Pharnaces II of Pontus
sources.note: King of Bosporus 63–47; Pompey 'named him a friend and ally' and declared Phanagoria 'to be independent'; 48–47 seized Colchis, Lesser Armenia, Pontus; Zela 47; Asander revolted and Pharnaces was killed in 47; Dynamis succeeded.

sources.title: Mithridates VI Eupator
sources.note: Fled 'to the lands north of the Black Sea in the winter of 66 BC'; Machares 'viceroy of Cimmerian Bosporus' killed; 'In 63 BC … Pharnaces II of Pontus, led a rebellion against his father'; suicide in the citadel of Panticapaeum; Chersonesus 'asked Mithridates VI to become its protector'.

sources.title: Tiberius Julius Cotys I
sources.note: Installed by Claudius in 45; deposed by Nero in 63; the kingdom 'incorporated as a part of the Roman Province of Moesia Inferior from 63 to 68'; Galba restored Rhescuporis in 68.

sources.title: Nymphaion (Crimea)
sources.note: Founded by Samians 580–560; Athens' 'principal military base in the region ca. 444 BC'; 'annexed to the Bosporan Kingdom by the end of the century'; Gylon's betrayal; 45.23667N 36.4175E.

sources.title: Feodosia
sources.note: Theodosia, Milesian colony of the 6th century BC; destroyed by the Huns in the 4th century; 45.034N 35.379E.

sources.title: Phanagoria
sources.note: Founded c. 543 BC by Teians; 'the eastern capital of the Bosporan Kingdom'; early 4th century BC the kingdom 'conquered much of Sindica, including the independent polis of Phanagoria'; allied with Rome and withstood Pharnaces II's siege; sacked by the Huns in the 4th century; 45.277N 36.966E.

sources.title: Gorgippia
sources.note: Anapa; Sindian Harbour, capital of Sindica; flourished as part of the kingdom in the 2nd–3rd centuries BC; 'inhabited until the 3rd century CE, when it was overrun by neighbouring native tribes'.

sources.title: Scythian Neapolis
sources.note: Capital of the Late Scythian kingdom in Crimea, end of the 3rd century BC to the second half of the 3rd century AD; destroyed by Diophantus and 'by the Goths halfway through the 3rd century AD'; 44.94278N 34.12056E.

sources.title: Asander (Bosporan king)
sources.note: Left in charge in 47 BC, revolted, Pharnaces killed; 'Sometime between 27 and 17 BC, Augustus formally recognised Asander as king'; wall of 360 stadia across the isthmus; died 17 BC; Scribonius, then Polemon I (to 8 BC), then Aspurgus.

sources.title: Dynamis (Bosporan queen)
sources.note: Roman client queen; married Polemon not before 17/16 BC; Polemon 'ruled until 8 BC', sacked Tanais, renamed Phanagoria Agrippia; Dynamis ruled alone again 8 BC–AD 7/8.

sources.title: Rhescuporis VI
sources.note: 'the last well-known king of the Bosporan Kingdom (r. 314–341)'; coin production ends 341; 'the Goths took power over at least parts of the Bosporan Kingdom c. 380', 'likely followed by a Hunnic invasion'; next attested king Douptounos (inscription dated 483).

sources.title: Tiberius Julius Mithridates
sources.note: Mithridates III, r. 39–44/45; deposed by Claudius in 45 for Cotys I; afterwards a 'three-day war' at the Don won by Cotys and the Roman eques Aquila (undated); Didius Gallus' garrison withdrawn.

sources.title: Sindi people
sources.note: Taman peninsula and the adjacent coast; kings Hecataeus and Octamasades c. 400 BC; 'Sindica was annexed by the Bosporan Kingdom during the reign of Leucon I, probably in the 380s BC'; governed by Gorgippus.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Cimmerian Bosporus' (-404..372) is the Bosporan Kingdom, which the page dates c. 480/438 BC – c. AD 527 with Panticapaeum as capital. One state throughout: the dynasty changes (Archaeanactids to Spartocids 438, Mithridates VI 107, Pharnaces II and the Roman clientship 63, Asander 47, Dynamis/Polemon 17, the Tiberian-Julian kings from Aspurgus) are recorded as rename events, not as separate states, so the row is not split. Three things are changed against Cliopatria: the start is moved from 404 to 480 (new keyframe); the two gaps (-91..-64 and 68..77) are filled; and the end is moved from 372 to 527 with a soft, core-only shape (373..527), because the kingdom's end under Rhescuporis VI 'is a matter of thin evidence' and the page runs it to Justinian. Territorial corrections: Sindica/Taman is added to the -383 shape (annexed by Leukon I 'probably in the 380s'); Phanagoria is removed at -63 (Pompey's free city) and returned under Polemon (confidence 1); Roman Chersonesus (Sevastopol, 35 km) is removed from the 78 and 371 shapes; the Crimean interior (Scythian Neapolis) is removed at 78 and regained in 193 (Sauromates II). Disagreements: Tanais is 'founded late in the 3rd century BC' on its own page but 'taken' by Paerisades I (349–310) on the Spartocid page; Cliopatria's -230 date is kept. Spartokos I ends 431 on the Bosporan page and 433 on the king list; Leukon I is 387–347 or 389–349; Paerisades V's death is 111 (list) or 108 (Spartocid page); Cotys I is 45–63 (his page) or 46–78 (list) — the list's dates are used in rulers, with notes. Not modelled: Chersonesus' call to Mithridates c. 110 (it became Pontic, then Roman — the Greek city-states dossier removes it from the poleis at -110); the Roman-backed war of Cotys I and Aquila against the deposed Mithridates III at the Don (a 'three-day war', undated on his page); the Alan/Sarmatian and Gothic overlordships after 341 (undated on the pages, so no vassal pairs); Gorgippia's loss to 'neighbouring native tribes' in the 3rd century AD (undated). Counterparts without a dossier: 'Sindi kingdom', 'Maeotian tribes', 'Phanagoria (free city)', 'Crimean Scythians', 'Eumelos (pretender)', 'Siraces', 'Theodosia' are name strings. 'goths' (Cliopatria 30..206) and 'huns' (106..425) are slugs whose shapes do not cover 330/372 in Crimea; the eastern-roman-empire dossier exists. Gazetteer: Sevastopol, Simferopol, Kerch, Tmutarakan, Azov, Colchis, Lesser Armenia, Pontus and the Kuban river resolve; Theodosia/Feodosia, Phanagoria, Gorgippia/Anapa, Nymphaion, Tanais and Panticapaeum do not and are given as coordinates from their pages.
